decisive_items: 50% to 90% diffuse stenosis in proximal to mid-LAD
ST-segment elevation and fusion with R waves in leads I, aVL, and V1 to V5
response.rationale: Coronary angiography demonstrates severe multivessel coronary artery disease, and the Holter shows polymorphic VT with ischemic ST-segment changes, directly supporting coronary artery disease as the cause of syncope. The normal QTc and normal echocardiogram exclude long QT syndrome and cardiomyopathy, respectively.

rejected.why: Ischemic cardiomyopathy is not supported because the ejection fraction is normal (58%) and there is no evidence of heart failure or structural cardiomyopathy.
ARVC is unlikely given the absence of right ventricular structural abnormalities and the presence of significant coronary artery disease that better explains the polymorphic VT.
Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is not supported by the normal echocardiogram and the absence of left ventricular hypertrophy or outflow tract obstruction.
Long QT syndrome is excluded because the QTc is normal (403 ms), and the polymorphic VT is better explained by ischemia.
Acquired long QT syndrome is not supported by the normal QTc and the presence of severe coronary artery disease.
